market_holds: XYF is no longer trading on its own earnings. On 2026-11-06 its controlling shareholder, Mangrove Coast Investment (affiliated with Chairman and CEO Justin Tang, about 93.45% of the voting power), made a preliminary non-binding going-private proposal at US$6.03 per ADS. The stock gapped +14% and closed +22% at 5.75 on 436k shares (Yahoo bars). A special committee of three independent directors was formed on 2026-11-18 (panabee summary of the 6-K). No advisors, financing or definitive agreement have been reported. Spot is 5.23 at today's close (Yahoo), a 15.3% discount to the offer, and wider than the 4.6% spread on Nov 6. Since Nov 6 the listed Chinese online-lending peers fell hard: QFIN 5.58 to 4.16 (-25%), LX 0.66 to 0.47 (-29%), FINV 2.94 to 2.37 (-19%). XYF fell only 5.75 to 5.23 (-9%), so it carries roughly a third of the peers' move through the fallback value. QFIN reported Q3 on 11-24 after the close and fell 9.8% today on 5.1M shares, LX fell 9.6% and FINV 4.4% on 4M; XYF was unchanged at 5.23 on 34k shares. There is no option market, and the baseline holds no earnings history (deadband 5.44% from 86% annualised 20-day vol). The pre-proposal prints moved hard and mostly down, from Yahoo bars: Q3-25 on 2025-11-21 -15.7%, 2026-03-26 -26.2% (Q4-25), 2026-05-22 -8.8% (Q1-26), and Q2-26 on 2026-08-24 +2%. No consensus or guide was found: XYF gave no Q3 guide in the Q2 release. Q2-26 (2026-08-24): facilitation RMB11.63bn (-20.5% QoQ, -70% YoY), non-GAAP NI RMB165.8m (+104% QoQ), 31-60d delinquency 1.73% vs 2.61%, 91-180d 9.09% vs 9.95%. The buyback (US$35.5m left) expires 2026-11-30; the semi-annual dividend comes with Q2/Q4 prints, not Q3. The report day is the Friday after Thanksgiving, a half session ending 13:00 ET, which is also the scoring time.
view: This print is an earnings release inside a pending controller take-private, so the reaction is decided by what it does to deal confidence and to the fallback value, not by the quarter's numbers. The bid caps the upside near 6.03: only a definitive agreement or a bump closes the spread, and neither is likely to land with the release, because the committee was formed only on Nov 18. The downside stays open through the fallback. Fresh dated read-through says the fallback is still falling. QFIN on 11-24 described 'clear erosion in risk performance' and an 'industry-wide liquidity squeeze' with tighter funding. It guided Q4 non-GAAP NI down 67-77% YoY and said regulatory uncertainty runs into 2027, and the sector sold off 4-10% today on it. XYF depends on funding partners and is smaller, so its Q3 most likely shows facilitation down again and credit no longer improving, against its own Q2, where credit had turned better and profit doubled QoQ. XYF did not move with peers today; the bid absorbs it. A weak quarter therefore probably nudges the spread wider, through a lower fallback and a small fear that a 93% controller re-cuts the price. A decent quarter barely lifts a capped stock. So I lean mildly down with a small expected size, likely inside the 5.44% deadband on a thin half-day session. That is not enough to recommend.
unpriced: Possibly the read-through from QFIN's 11-24 print and today's sector sell-off: XYF's price did not move today, because the take-private bid anchors it. But the anchor is the reason the print matters little either way, so the gap is small and asymmetric (capped upside, open downside) rather than a clear mispricing.

recommendation.reason: The stock trades on a US$6.03 controller take-private bid, which caps the upside and compresses any earnings reaction. QFIN's 11-24 print and today's 4-10% peer sell-off point to a weak sector Q3, which tilts the open downside slightly, but the link from results to deal confidence is weak and the expected move sits inside the deadband on a thin half-day session. The direction lean falls short of the 65 bar.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: The release carrying deal news: a definitive merger agreement or a committee advisor and process update (up toward 6.03), or a revised or withdrawn proposal (sharply down).

self_critique: The bid may make the print almost irrelevant: arb holders support any dip toward a 15% spread, and the release will likely repeat that the committee is evaluating, giving a move inside the deadband with a sign that is noise. XYF also shrank earlier than its peers. Its Q2 showed credit improving and profit doubling QoQ, so its Q3 could look better than QFIN's, and a profitable quarter lowers the perceived risk that the controller walks away. Against that, the dated evidence (QFIN's guide, today's sector sell-off) lowers the fallback, while the upside is capped by the offer price. That asymmetry is real but small, so I keep the mild lean and make no call.
approach_notes: P4/P6 (tie each move to its news, take the run-in apart against peers) were what exposed the take-private bid and the capped upside; without it this would have read as a high-vol print stock with -9 to -26% history. The playbook has no guidance on names under a pending bid, where the deciding line is deal confidence rather than the quarter.
